finalText:
Done. `POST /orders/:id/apply-coupon` is implemented, type-checked, and tested.

What I changed:

- [orderService.ts](/work/src/services/orderService.ts) — new `applyCoupon(id, couponCode)` holding all the business rules: REQ-13 validation, then the exact error-precedence order (order exists → PENDING → no coupon yet → coupon exists → ACTIVE → validity window → usage limit → minimum amount), the FIXED/PERCENT discount math with the max-discount and amount caps, and storing the normalized upper-case code. Time comes from the injected `Clock`, and all comparisons are inclusive/exclusive per REQ-03.
- [orderRepository.ts](/work/src/repositories/orderRepository.ts) — a single `applyCoupon` method that runs the order update, the `coupon_redemptions` insert, and the `used_count + 1` in one `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` transaction, rolling back on any failure. It stays in the repository layer so SQL is not leaked into services, and keeps all three writes atomic (REQ-12).
- [routes/orders.ts](/work/src/routes/orders.ts) and [app.ts](/work/src/app.ts) — the route just parses the id/body and delegates; wiring passes the coupon repository into `OrderService` (appended as the third parameter so the existing `(orders, clock)` order is preserved).
- [applyCoupon.test.ts](/work/tests/applyCoupon.test.ts) — 17 new tests covering all ten acceptance criteria plus error precedence, and a check that a rejected request leaves the order, `used_count`, and `coupon_redemptions` untouched. The existing test file is unchanged.

`npm run build` and `npm test` both pass (22 tests across the two files).
